clue.text: Expert contracted to provide cover had issue

indicators.note: the word for contracted wraps round, covering, the word for expert

parts.note: contracted means reduced, made smaller
a pro is an expert, a professional

explanation.surface: A specialist hired on a short contract to stand in for someone ran into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had issue' reads as 'had a problem', but issue here means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To have issue is to produce children, which is the biological sense of reproducing.

clue.text: Write and ask when disposed to do sport

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters of the two words are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: An invitation to write in and ask whenever you feel like taking up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' looks like 'inclined', as in 'disposed to do sport', but it signals rearranging the letters of WRITE and ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimming across water on skis towed by a boat is a sporting activity, so the verb means doing that sport.

clue.text: Call from dove about to carry lemur

indicators.note: the dove's call goes round, about, the word for carry

parts.note: a dove's call is a coo
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A dove's call is about to carry off a lemur.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is the flying lemur of South-East Asia, a gliding mammal that is not a true lemur.
explanation.definitionFit: The gliding mammal of South-East Asian forests is commonly called the flying lemur.

clue.text: Count places restriction on king

indicators.note: in a down answer, the restriction is placed on top of the king

parts.note: a ban is a restriction
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An earl or count imposes limits on a monarch's power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but it is a verb, as in 'count on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to count on or rely on it.

clue.text: Fact about soil conditioner mostly broken down

indicators.note: the word for fact goes round the shortened soil conditioner

parts.note: a deed is a fact, as in 'in deed'

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the soil conditioner is used

parts.note: compost is rotted matter dug in to improve soil

explanation.surface: A gardening truth about compost that has largely rotted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the T of COMPOST; DEED gives fact through the phrase 'in deed', meaning in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic matter that has rotted has been broken down by decay into simpler substances.

clue.text: Brave leader upset over child for instance

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a minor is a child in law
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A chief was distressed by a child, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' was the old term for a Native American warrior; this Apache leader is famous for resisting the US army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache war leader who fought the US and Mexico was a leader of braves, Native American warriors.

clue.text: Streetcar crossing close to you a shock

indicators.note: the tram goes across, around, the letter taken from you

parts.note: a streetcar is the American word for a tram

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A streetcar crossing your path would give you a nasty fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' puts U, the last letter of 'you', inside TRAM, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological trauma is a deep emotional shock, often after a disturbing event.

clue.text: Virile man takes time in French south

indicators.note: the French word for south takes, holds, the time abbreviation

parts.note: sud is the French for south

explanation.surface: A macho man spends some time in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexually potent, virile man, from the breeding stallion.

clue.text: Bats are able to develop

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Bats can evolve, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the subject of the sentence, the animals, but it is the adjective meaning mad, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on an idea is to develop it in greater detail.

clue.text: Bird eating fish, Ruth wants no starter

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or sorrow, so regret

explanation.surface: A bird is eating fish, and someone called Ruth is not interested in a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name but is the old noun for sorrow, the root of 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender white heron hunts in shallow water, a fish-eating wading bird.

clue.text: Having green eggs first as does partner

indicators.note: the eggs come first, ahead of the slang word for green

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
green is slang for money; a buck is a US dollar, a greenback

explanation.surface: Someone eats green eggs to start the day, just as their partner does.
explanation.walkthrough: Unpunctuated, 'as does partner' reads as 'like the partner does'; it means the male partner of does, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The male roe deer mates with the females, called does, so he is their partner.

clue.text: Ring round being pompous

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped
rotund means round, plump

explanation.surface: A circle is round, which is a pompous way of putting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund speech is grandiloquent and inflated, so the word describes pompous talk.

clue.text: Dance record broke in middle

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the middle letter of broke is taken

explanation.surface: A dance record snapped in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is an event where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Agent with staff brought in to deliver carpet

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent

indicators.note: the word for staff is brought into the word for deliver

parts.note: to rid is to deliver or free
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: An agent arrives with workers to deliver a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like the delivery, a rug, but it is the verb meaning to tell off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in to be rebuked, to reprimand.

clue.text: Go for broke on forest where domestic growth high?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the forest
broke means broken, so these letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland of Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: Go all out on a forest where home-grown plants shoot up high?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go for broke' looks like the idiom for risking all, but 'broke' scrambles GO FOR into ROOFG.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grown on top of a house are domestic growth high above the ground.

clue.text: Fantasist armed and ready for manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres move troops about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A fantasist is armed and ready for military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in daydreams indulges in fantasies, so a fantasist.

clue.text: Corrupt economist prayed for moral guidance

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked economist prayed for moral guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as describing the economist, but it signals scrambling ECONOMIST PRAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is a moral lesson: wrongdoing never pays off, guidance against crime.

clue.text: Be harbouring monster? Here's one to help!

indicators.note: the word for be holds, harbours, the monster

parts.note: to be is to exist
an orc is a monster of fantasy, as in Tolkien

explanation.surface: Possessed by a monster? This person can help you!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the first half: someone harbouring a demon is just who this helper aids.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest who drives out evil spirits helps someone possessed by a demon.

clue.text: Pair touring Canada pranged station wagon?

indicators.note: the pair abbreviation goes round, touring, the scrambled letters
pranged means crashed, so the letters are smashed up

explanation.surface: A couple touring Canada crashed their estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station wagon' looks like an estate car but here means a police-station vehicle. A panda car is the British police patrol car, named for its black-and-white livery.
explanation.definitionFit: A British police patrol car belongs to a police station, a wagon of the station.

clue.text: Forcibly removed due to Masonic transgression?

definitions.meaning: Freemasons meet in lodges, so one expelled for misconduct would be thrown out of the lodge

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out because of a Freemason's misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DIS-LODGED: removed from a Masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shifted from a fixed place by force has been ousted from its position.

clue.text: Wanted to find variety on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so a word is said aloud

parts.note: a sort is a variety or kind

explanation.surface: Wanted to find a variety show on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, SORT and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past of seek, so something sought was looked for, wanted.

clue.text: Medic claiming single fare from Turkey

indicators.note: the doctor abbreviation claims, takes in, the number

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
single means one

explanation.surface: A doctor charges for a one-way ticket out of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price but means food; doner kebab is Turkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Doner kebab, spit-roasted meat sliced thin, is a Turkish dish, food from that country.

clue.text: Welshman and Scotsman in spirit guarding place

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for Dafydd
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A Welshman and a Scotsman are full of spirit as they guard a place.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek belief a daimon is a minor deity; Collins gives the guardian spirit of a place or person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek religion this minor deity could be the guardian spirit of a person or locality.

clue.text: Lively ball requires tough doorman

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a fast short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batter
a heavy who guards a nightclub door and ejects troublemakers

explanation.surface: A lively party needs a hard man on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' looks like a dance; in cricket it is a delivery that rears up off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same word: the rearing cricket delivery and the club's heavy.

clue.text: Worker perhaps rejoices at first pint

parts.note: a worker bee is one kind of bee, hence perhaps

indicators.note: the first letter of rejoices is taken

explanation.surface: A worker celebrates with his first pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is a worker bee, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is the standard measure of ale served in a British pub, so a drink of it.

clue.text: All family members at home in Scots island?

parts.words: All family members at home in Scots
parts.note: read backwards from the answer: O (zero, none) plus KIN plus AWA' (Scots for away) says 'no relatives away', which is everyone at home

explanation.surface: Is a Scottish island where the whole family is at home?
explanation.walkthrough: This works in reverse: split the answer into O, KIN and AWA', Scots for away, and it says 'zero kin away', so all the family are home. 'Scots' points at the dialect, not the island's location.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Ryukyu chain in southern Japan is a well-known Pacific island.

clue.text: I've messed up in no surgical procedures!

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, so it stands for no
ops is short for operations, surgical procedures

explanation.surface: A surgeon's confession: a blunder with no operations to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone blurts on making a small blunder, admitting a mistake.

clue.text: English army getting back to front shows spirit

indicators.note: the back letter of the army word moves to the front

parts.note: a host is an army, a multitude

explanation.surface: An English army's rearguard moves up front and shows its mettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' does not reverse HOST; only its last letter moves to the front, giving THOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit of a community or enterprise.

clue.text: ESP in later years to keep old in hush-hush work

parts.note: extrasensory perception, taken as written

indicators.note: the word in keeps, holds, the abbreviation for old

parts.note: age means one's later years, old age

explanation.surface: Telepathy in old age keeps a veteran in secret work.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is secret, hush-hush work done for a government or company.
